states.name: Alaska
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No UA Board of Regents or state action on reduced-credit bachelor’s degrees found; P10.04.030 still sets a 120-credit minimum (a presidential exception route exists).
states.framework: Each MAU must have a common core of general education requirements of at least 34 credits, distributed among categories set in University Regulation; the core is the minimum general education curriculum for baccalaureate degrees.

states.name: Alabama
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No ACHE or legislative action on reduced-credit (about 90-credit) bachelor’s degrees found. SACSCOC (the regional accreditor) opened a reduced-credit pathway, but no Alabama state body has acted.
states.framework: AGSC statewide General Studies Curriculum, Areas I-IV: Written Composition 6, Humanities and Fine Arts 12 (incl. 3 literature, 3 arts), Natural Sciences and Mathematics 11 (3 math, 8 science with lab), History, Social and Behavioral Sciences 12; maximum total 41-42 SH; Area V = pre-major courses. Engineering variant cuts Areas II and IV to 9 SH each.

states.name: Arkansas
states.label: proposal, directive or study
states.action: ADHE taskforce report ‘Charting a Course through Reduced Credit’ (December 2025, posted 2026) recommends a measured approach: pilot parameters, distinct nomenclature, financial-aid analysis, and review of the state core. No AHECB policy change found. Institution level: Arkansas Tech University trustees approved cutting the BA in Organizational Leadership from 120 to 90 credits (October 2025), pending ADHE and HLC approval (news snippet, unverified).
states.framework: AHECB State Minimum General Education Core, 35 SCH, required in all transferable associate degrees and all bachelor’s degrees; includes a 15-16 SCH Requisite Core (English/communication, math or science, US History, American Government) created by Act 566 of 2025. Distribution: English Composition 6, Speech 0-3, Mathematics 3, Science with labs 8, Fine Arts/Humanities 6-9, American Government 3, US History 3, Social Sciences 3-6. Engineering majors may take higher-level math/science and substitute 6 upper-level humanities/social science hours.

states.name: Arizona
states.label: programs approved at public institutions
states.action: Arizona State University created 90-credit, three-year Bachelor of Education degrees (Elementary Education; Special Education): approved by the ASU University Senate on March 2, 2026 (82 to 27), described by ASU as accredited through HLC, launched August 27, 2026 (online start Oct. 14, 2026; immersion Jan. 11, 2027), also offered with Arizona Western College. No Arizona Board of Regents vote or policy change specific to reduced-credit degrees was located; ABOR 2-223 requires Board approval for new degree programs but sets no 120-credit floor.
states.framework: ABOR Policy 2-210 General Education: each university must have general education requirements of at least 32 semester credits, distributed across Literature; Fine Arts and Humanities; Social and Behavioral Sciences; American Institutions (incl. economics and US history); Natural Sciences; Composition, Communication and Rhetoric; Mathematics and Quantitative Reasoning. Completed AGEC (Arizona General Education Curriculum, 35-credit block, AGEC-A subject areas total 32-35) satisfies the university general education requirement for transfer students.

states.name: California
states.label: board or system policy adopted
states.action: May 4-6, 2026: CSU Board of Trustees adopted Title 5 amendments (REP 05-26-02) creating the Bachelor of Education, Bachelor of Professional Studies and Bachelor of Applied Studies, which may be offered as reduced-credit baccalaureate degrees (RCBDs) of 90 to 120 semester units; residence rules also relaxed. Campuses choose whether to offer them; no mandate. Amendments to be filed with the Office of Administrative Law. BA and BS degrees stay at 120 units. No state legislation and no specific approved campus programs found.
states.framework: CSU General Education Requirements: at least 43 semester units, including 9 upper-division units (9 English communication and critical thinking, 13 science and quantitative reasoning, 9 arts and humanities, 9 social sciences, 3 ethnic studies); community college transfers may meet GE with Cal-GETC (34 lower-division units) plus 9 upper-division units = 43

states.name: Colorado
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No CCHE policy change, program approval, pilot or statute on 90-credit bachelor’s degrees found in CCHE commission agendas and minutes from June 2025 to November 2026. The only item: the June 11, 2026 CCHE agenda (May 2026 minutes) records that faculty advisor Artis reported on a statewide faculty survey about 90-credit bachelor’s degrees.
states.framework: gtPathways (Guaranteed Transfer Pathways) general education curriculum: 31 credits in six categories (written communication, mathematics, arts and humanities, history, social and behavioral sciences, natural and physical sciences); the core of gen ed in most liberal arts and sciences bachelor’s degrees; statute requires a core of 30 to 40 credit hours

states.name: Connecticut
states.label: proposal, directive or study
states.action: Raised Bill SB 396 (February Session 2026) would amend CGS 10a-34 so the Office of Higher Education accepts applications for degree programs of not fewer than 90 credits; referred to the Higher Education and Employment Advancement Committee (March 3, 2026), public hearing March 10, 2026; no further action recorded (not enacted).
states.framework: CSCU Framework 30 (FW30): 30-credit categorical general education curriculum for transfer associate degrees at CT State; CSCU four-year institutions must apply FW30-mapped courses to their own general education core (BOR Policy 1.26, June 27, 2024). Transfer and Articulation Policy (TAP) pathways.

states.name: District of Columbia
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No UDC Board of Trustees or DC government action on reduced-credit bachelor’s degrees found.
states.framework: UDC Interdisciplinary General Education Program (IGED), 13 courses; standard 37 credits for bachelor’s degrees; some programs specify other IGED sets (40, 34, 31, or 28 credits plus substitutions; BS Civil Engineering lists 34).

states.name: Delaware
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No state-level action on reduced-credit bachelor’s degrees found.
states.framework: None statewide; UD and DSU each set their own general education requirements.

states.name: Florida
states.label: proposal, directive or study
states.action: BOG noticed an amendment to Regulation 8.014 on Sept. 3, 2026 (comment period closed Sept. 17, 2026) letting the Board approve trustee requests for undergraduate degree programs requiring fewer than 120 credit hours, with criteria: upper-division rigor, full 36-credit general education and civic literacy, articulation, distinct program designation, student disclosure, transfer into the traditional program, annual outcome reports. An earlier notice of intent went to the Board on June 25, 2026. Final adoption pending (next Board meeting Nov. 12-13, 2026; agenda not posted on 2026-10-29). No minimum credit floor stated.
states.framework: Statewide general education core: at least one core course in each of 5 areas (communication, mathematics, social sciences, humanities, natural sciences; 5 courses x 3 credits = 15 core credits) within 36 total general education semester hours; plus 6 extra writing-intensive credits, civic literacy course and assessment, foreign language (admission requirement or before graduation), 9 summer credits for students entering with fewer than 60 hours

states.name: Georgia
states.label: board or system policy adopted
states.action: August 2026: University System of Georgia Board of Regents changed its guidelines to allow 90-credit Bachelor of Applied Science degrees in high-demand workforce areas; no program named as of 5 November 2026
states.framework: USG Core IMPACTS general education: 42 credit hours across seven areas (Institutional Priority; Mathematics and Quantitative Skills; Political Science and U.S. History; Arts, Humanities and Ethics; Communicating in Writing; Technology, Mathematics and Sciences; Social Sciences), plus 18 hours of Field of Study prerequisites; required in AA, AS, BA and BS degrees and transferable within USG

states.name: Hawaii
states.label: board or system policy adopted
states.action: UH system executive policy EP 5.205 (July 2026) defines the Bachelor of Professional Studies (B.P.S.) as typically offered in reduced-credit formats of 90 credits or more; EP 5.201 (June 2026) notes WSCUC will review reduced-credit bachelor’s proposals as a new degree level. No specific UH reduced-credit program approval found.
states.framework: UH 10-campus System General Education, 31 credits: Written Communication 3, Quantitative Reasoning 3, Hawaiian Knowledge 3, Biological Science 3, Physical Science 3, Science Lab 1, Global and Multicultural Perspectives 3, Arts/Humanities/Literature 3, Social Sciences 3, plus two more courses (6). Campuses may add at most 12 credits of graduation requirements for a bachelor’s (excluding Hawaiian or second language).

states.name: Iowa
states.label: law enacted
states.action: House File 440 (2025, ‘College Affordability Act’) added Iowa Code 262.9(39) directing each Regent university to begin efforts to offer at least one baccalaureate degree program that can be completed in three years. On June 16, 2026 the Board of Regents approved (consent agenda, Academic Affairs Committee recommendation) a new reduced-credit degree type, the Bachelor of Applied Professional Studies (BAPS), at ISU, UI and UNI: 90-95 credits, general education core, HLC approval required; individual BAPS programs expected for Board approval in 2026-27.
states.framework: None systemwide for the bachelor’s degree; each Regent university sets its own general education program. The reduced-credit BAPS framework requires a ‘General Education core’ without a credit number.

states.name: Idaho
states.label: board or system policy adopted
states.action: SBOE amended Policy III.E (first reading October 2025, adopted December 2025) to add a Reduced-Credit Baccalaureate Degree: at least 90 semester credits, including at least 36 general education credits and 36 upper-division credits, limited to workforce-focused circumstances, titles must flag reduced credit. On December 17, 2025 the Board approved ISU reduced-credit (3YR) BAS programs (Applied Business and Professional Sales; Intelligent and Trustworthy Digital Systems; Law Enforcement Management and Leadership); ISU launched them May 2026 as Idaho’s first public three-year bachelor’s degrees. An October 2026 redline would add a documented employer-need test.
states.framework: Statewide General Education framework (GEM): at least 31 credits in GEM competency areas plus at least 5 institutionally designated credits; distribution: Written Communication 6, Oral Communication 3, Mathematical 3, Scientific 7 (two disciplines, one lab), Humanistic and Artistic 6, Social and Behavioral 6, Institutional 5 = 36. Applies to AA, AS and baccalaureate degrees.

states.name: Illinois
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No IBHE, ICCB or General Assembly action on reduced-credit bachelor’s degrees was found (IBHE press releases, calendar and legislative-report pages checked). The 120-credit minimum in 23 Ill. Adm. Code 1050.30 would block 90-credit programs at public universities without a rule change.
states.framework: Illinois Articulation Initiative General Education Core Curriculum (IAI GECC) package: 12 to 13 courses, 37 to 41 semester credit hours (Communication 9; Humanities and Fine Arts 9; Mathematics 3 to 5; Physical and Life Sciences 7 to 8 with a lab; Social and Behavioral Sciences 9). A completed package transfers as a block in place of the receiving institution’s lower-division general education; it does not set a minimum for the bachelor’s degree.

states.name: Indiana
states.label: law enacted
states.action: IC 21-41-15 (enacted 2024): by Nov. 1, 2024 each state educational institution offering baccalaureate degrees must adopt a policy to review the feasibility of offering each four-year program in a structure completable in three years (CHE sets guidance); by July 1, 2025 each must offer at least one baccalaureate program specifically structured for full-time completion within three years (with coaching, experiential or work-based learning, and no dual-credit prerequisite); annual reports to CHE from Nov. 1, 2025; CHE may count three-year completions in the outcomes-based funding formula. The statute does not set a credit total, so these programs may be 120 credits on an accelerated schedule (“Degree-in-3”) rather than 90-credit degrees.
states.framework: Indiana Statewide Transfer General Education Core (STGEC, now branded the Indiana College Core): at least 30 credit hours built on six competencies (Foundational Intellectual Skills: written communication, speaking and listening, quantitative reasoning; Ways of Knowing: scientific, social and behavioral, humanistic and artistic), at least 3 credits in each; transfers as a block among state institutions. CHE guidance: each state educational institution must offer a general education program of at least 30 credit hours that addresses these competencies.

states.name: Kansas
states.label: board or system policy adopted
states.action: After K-State proposed a 90-hour uncrewed aircraft systems degree (September 2025), KBOR formed a task force; on June 17, 2026 the Board adopted policy allowing institutions to pilot Reduced Credit Baccalaureate Degrees (at least 90 SCH, 34 SCH gen ed, 34 upper-division SCH, approval limited to three academic years, transcript and diploma notation). No individual program approvals found yet.
states.framework: KBOR Systemwide General Education framework, 34-35 credit hours in seven buckets: English 6, Communication 3, Math and Statistics 3, Natural and Physical Sciences 4-5 (one lab course), Social and Behavioral Sciences 6, Arts and Humanities 6, Institutionally Designated 6; effective no later than fall 2024 for all baccalaureate degrees.

states.name: Kentucky
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No CPE policy or statute on reduced-credit bachelor’s degrees found. In a September 2026 CPE bulletin the CPE President asked institutional boards to consider accelerated bachelor’s degrees (exhortation, not a policy action). HB 427 (2025; would have made the 120 limit mandatory; last action to Senate Education 2/26/25) and HB 94 (2026; recommitted to House A&R 4/15/26) concerned the 120-hour limit and transfer pathways, not 90-credit degrees.
states.framework: CPE General Education Transfer Policy and Statewide General Education Core (effective fall 2012): minimum 30 unduplicated SCH for the general education component of a baccalaureate degree, in Communications 6-9, Quantitative Reasoning 3-6, Arts and Humanities 6-9, Natural Sciences 3-7, Social and Behavioral Sciences 6-9; category, core, and fully certified transfer levels.

states.name: Louisiana
states.label: board or system policy adopted
states.action: 2026-03-24: Board of Regents approved the Accelerated Baccalaureate (AccB) policy framework in AA Policy 2.15 (three-year, 90-hour degree with all AA 2.16 gen-ed elements, up to 12 gen-ed hours may be met by major coursework, embedded work-based learning, final approval by Regents, open to all four-year public institutions) and at the same meeting approved the first two AccB programs at LSU Alexandria (Bioinformatics, Information Technology). Programs also need SACSCOC approval; students may start courses in fall 2026.
states.framework: Statewide General Education Requirements: 39 hours for BA, BS and B degrees (33 for BAS): English composition 6, math/analytical reasoning 6, natural sciences 9, humanities 9, fine arts 3, social/behavioral sciences 6

states.name: Massachusetts
states.label: programs approved at public institutions
states.action: BHE voted on 2026-02-10 (two members opposed) to adopt 610 CMR 16.00, Degree Granting Regulations for Pilot Proposals on Innovation (motion BHE 26-28 first presented 2025-10-28), letting public and independent institutions propose pilots that depart from Board rules such as the 120-credit minimum. On 2026-06-26 the BHE approved the first pilots: Merrimack College (four applied bachelor’s degrees at 96 credits) and Suffolk University (about 94 credits), both private; programs to start fall 2027. No public institution pilot found yet.
states.framework: MassTransfer General Education Foundation (formerly MassTransfer Block): 34 credits (6 English composition/writing, 9 behavioral/social sciences, 9 humanities/fine arts, 7 natural/physical science, 3 mathematics/quantitative reasoning); 28-credit STEM Gen Ed Foundation for STEM A2B pathways. Transfer block, not a minimum for the public bachelor’s. Separately, 610 CMR 2.07(3)(c)2 sets a 36-credit general education minimum for baccalaureate degrees at independent institutions.

states.name: Maryland
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No MHEC or USM action on reduced-credit (about 90-credit) bachelor’s degrees found as of 2026-10-29; the 120-credit floor in COMAR 13B.02.02.16B(1)(a) applies to all in-State institutions.
states.framework: Bachelor’s general education program of at least 38 and not more than 48 credit hours across five core areas (arts and humanities, social and behavioral sciences, biological and physical sciences incl. one lab, mathematics, English composition); up to 8 institution-specific credits outside the five areas; each course at least 3 credits

states.name: Maine
states.label: programs approved at public institutions
states.action: January 2025: UMS Trustees authorized development of up to five 90-credit applied bachelor’s programs as a pilot for adult degree completers. July 14, 2025: Trustees unanimously approved five 90-credit applied bachelor’s programs as a pilot (enrollment limited to adult learners away at least two years; ‘Applied’ and ‘90-credit’ in degree names). November 2025: NECHE approved three (Applied Public Administration, UMA; Applied Business Management, UMFK; Applied Psychology, UMPI), active fall 2026. November 17, 2025: Trustees adopted Policy 316 Enrollment Safeguards for 90-Credit Programs.
states.framework: No systemwide general education minimum; each UMS university sets its own; Board Policy 304 governs transfer of credit.

states.name: Michigan
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No state-level (legislative or state agency) action found. Private institutions offer HLC-approved 90-credit bachelor’s degrees: Davenport University (applied marketing, fall 2026), Northwood University (cybersecurity, fall 2025), Adrian College (two business degrees), College for Creative Studies (fashion business management, fall 2026). No Michigan public university program was found.
states.framework: Michigan Transfer Agreement (MTA, MiTransfer): 30 semester hours with a grade of 2.0 or better in each course (English composition, communications, mathematics, social sciences, humanities and fine arts, natural sciences), satisfying a majority of lower-level general education at receiving institutions; replaced MACRAO for students entering fall 2014. Transfer block only; it does not set a minimum for the bachelor’s degree.

states.name: Minnesota
states.label: programs approved at public institutions
states.action: Minnesota Office of Higher Education (state agency) convened a 2025 working group and in January 2026 adopted revised Minnesota Academic Program Standards that add reduced-credit bachelor’s degrees (minimum 90 semester or 135 quarter credits, 30 gen-ed, 30 major, 36 upper-level). OHE-approved programs so far are at private institutions (Concordia University, Saint Paul BA Exercise Science launched January 2026, later expanded to nine programs after HLC approvals, April 2026; Saint Mary’s University of Minnesota). No change to the statutory 120-credit cap for Minnesota State found.
states.framework: Minnesota Transfer Curriculum (MnTC): 10 goal areas, minimum 40-credit MnTC package approved at each Minnesota State college and university and implemented to support its programs; entire MnTC transfers as complete. OHE Minnesota Academic Program Standards (Jan 2026) require at least 30 semester credits of general education for bachelor’s and reduced-credit bachelor’s degrees at OHE-reviewed institutions.

states.name: Missouri
states.label: programs approved at public institutions
states.action: MDHEWD/CBHE created a routine-review track and form for New Reduced Credit Hour Bachelor’s Program proposals (form dated Dec. 2025). Proposals posted for review in 2026: Missouri Western State BAS Criminal Justice (Mar. 2026), BAS Child Development and BAS Respiratory Care (Apr. 2026), Maryville University BS Accelerated Accounting at 90 credits (May 2026, private), and a batch of Southeast Missouri State reduced-credit-hour degrees (June 2026). Southeast Missouri State announced (2026-04-07) Missouri’s first 90-credit-hour BS in Criminal Justice starting fall 2026 after its Board of Regents approved it in May 2025 pending CBHE and HLC review.
states.framework: CORE 42: CBHE-developed recommended lower-division core transfer curriculum of 42 semester credit hours with MOTR common course numbering; transfers as a block among public institutions. Also 60-credit lower-division transfer blocks for five program areas (2025 amendment). Transfer curriculum, not a statutory minimum for the bachelor’s.

states.name: Mississippi
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No IHL Board action on reduced-credit bachelor’s degrees found; the March 2026 IHL Policies and Bylaws still set a 120-hour minimum with no reduced-credit provision. SACSCOC (accreditor) adopted a reduced-credit policy in 2025-2026, which does not count as state action.
states.framework: IHL Board core curriculum required for every baccalaureate: English Composition 6, College Algebra/Quantitative Reasoning or higher math 3, Natural Science 6, Humanities and Fine Arts 9, Social or Behavioral Science 6 (total 30 semester hours)

states.name: Montana
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No Board of Regents action on reduced-credit bachelor’s degrees found. Policy 301.11 was revised on 2025-11-21 (Item 221-101-R1125) to align degree definitions with NWCCU, keeping the 120-hour standard and adding outcomes-based and PLA language; no reduced-credit provision. Agendas of BOR and ARSA committee meetings from Sept. 2025 to Sept. 2026 showed no reduced-credit items.
states.framework: MUS Transferable Core: 30 credits; completing the full core guarantees no further lower-division gen-ed on transfer; each campus has its own approved general education program (Policy 301.11 requires a general education core consistent with 301.10). Transfer core, not a system minimum for the bachelor’s.

states.name: North Carolina
states.label: pilot opened
states.action: 27 April 2026: UNC Board of Governors opened a pilot of 90-credit degrees; 18 proposals from seven campuses, first programs possible in fall 2027; Appalachian State proposed construction management among 11 programs of 90 to 100 credits for associate-degree holders
states.framework: No UNC systemwide gen-ed minimum; each university sets its gen-ed curriculum in its catalog. Statewide transfer block: Comprehensive Articulation Agreement (CAA) with the NC Community College System, including the Universal General Education Transfer Component (UGETC); students with an NC community college AA or AS receive a General Education Waiver at any UNC institution

states.name: North Dakota
states.label: pilot opened
states.action: SBHE approved Policies 409 and 409.1 in January 2026 allowing NDUS institutions to pilot reduced-credit bachelor’s degrees: up to two pilots per institution, Bachelor of Applied Science only, workforce-aligned, no licensure-track programs, employer support, tracking; sunset/reassessment in 2030. In April 2026 (vote reported 2026-04-30) the SBHE unanimously approved the first pilot: Dickinson State University’s 90-credit BAS in Management, pending HLC approval. Earlier (Oct. 2025) Valley City State, Mayville State and Bismarck State had programs outlined, incl. a 106-credit VCSU education degree.
states.framework: General Education Requirements Transfer Agreement (GERTA): systemwide agreement letting students complete gen-ed at any NDUS campus or ND tribal college and transfer it as a block. Credit total not verified (hint: 38). Transfer agreement, not a stated system minimum for the bachelor’s.

states.name: Nebraska
states.label: programs approved at public institutions
states.action: NSCS Board of Trustees discussed 90-credit degree pathways (2025-09-11); on 2026-01-15 approved revisions to Policy 4140 adding a Reduced Credit Baccalaureate Degree (BA/BS in Applied ..., minimum 90 credits) and approved Chadron State’s BA Applied Justice Studies and BS Applied Education reduced-credit programs (minutes, motions passed). Further reduced-credit proposals on later agendas: Wayne State BS/BA Applied Business Administration (90 credits, Apr. 2026, contingent on HLC), WSC BS Applied Special Education and BS Applied Elementary Education, Peru State BS Applied Business Administration and BS Applied Criminal Justice (June 2026), WSC Applied Criminal Justice (Nov. 2026). CCPE and HLC approval also required.
states.framework: NSCS general studies program of 30 to 37 credit hours aligned to college learning outcomes (up to 40 with an upper-division capstone; BAS gen studies max 30)

states.name: New Hampshire
states.label: programs approved at public institutions
states.action: 30 July 2026: University of New Hampshire (public) launched two online 90-credit applied bachelor's degrees
states.framework: No statewide gen-ed minimum found; set by each institution. USNH Administrative Board academic policies (USY II) cover only honorary degrees and tuition waivers.

states.name: New Jersey
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No OSHE rule change or state approval of reduced-credit bachelor’s degrees found; N.J.A.C. 9A:1-2.4(a) still requires at least 120 credits.
states.framework: Lampitt Law (P.L. 2007, c.175) statewide transfer agreement: completed AA/AS from a county college transfers as the first two years of a bachelor’s at NJ public four-year institutions, with a general education core listed by the Presidents’ Council. N.J.A.C. 9A:1-2.3: AA gen-ed at least 33 credits, AS at least 30. N.J.A.C. 9A:1-2.4(b): approximately half of the 120 baccalaureate credits shall be general education.

states.name: New Mexico
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No NMHED rule change or program approval for reduced-credit bachelor’s degrees found.
states.framework: Statewide general education curriculum of 31 credit hours for all bachelor’s and AA/AS degrees: Fixed 22 (communications, mathematics, science, social and behavioral science, humanities, creative and fine arts) plus Flexible 9 set by each institution; AAS 15 credits. Department must adopt at least 30 credits.

states.name: Nevada
states.label: proposal, directive or study
states.action: Board of Regents Academic, Research and Student Affairs Committee agenda 2026-03-05, item 11 Time-to-Degree Innovation in Baccalaureate Programs (information only): staff presentation on reduced-credit baccalaureate programs and the national landscape, with Weber State University on its 90-credit strategies. No policy change or program approval found in 2025-2026 Board agendas.
states.framework: NSHE System General Education Requirements for AA, AS, AB and baccalaureate graduates: English 3-6 (incl. ENG 102), Mathematics 3, Natural Science 6 (one lab), Social Sciences or Humanities/Fine Arts 9; total 21-24 credits; plus U.S. and Nevada Constitutions (NRS 396.500). BAS/AAS: 18 credits. Institutions set the rest of their gen-ed.

states.name: New York
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No NYSED, Board of Regents, SUNY or CUNY action on reduced-credit (about 90-credit) bachelor’s degrees was found. The 120-semester-hour floor in 8 NYCRR 52.2(c)(7) remains (3.47 last amended eff. 2/26/2025, not on this point). Bills found in the 2025-2026 session (e.g., S6696, A3693) concern Regents-exam credit and CUNY-to-SUNY transfer, not three-year degrees.
states.framework: SUNY General Education Framework (SUNY GE): at least 30 credits of SUNY GE-approved liberal arts and sciences, at least 7 of 10 knowledge and skills areas (Communication, Diversity: Equity, Inclusion and Social Justice, Mathematics, Natural Sciences required) plus 2 core competencies, completable within the first 60 credits, for all AA, AS and baccalaureate programs (effective fall 2023). CUNY Pathways: 30-credit Common Core (12 Required, 18 Flexible) for AA, AS and bachelor’s students, plus 6 to 12 College Option credits for bachelor’s students (36 to 42 total). NYSED 8 NYCRR 3.47(c) liberal arts share: BA three quarters of the work, BS one half, specialized degrees (B.E., B.Tech., B.Arch., B.B.A., B.P.S. etc.) one quarter.

states.name: Ohio
states.label: law enacted
states.action: HB 184 (136th General Assembly), effective 2026-03-20: ORC 3345.89 creates the Accelerated College and Career Pathways Program; each state university must establish at least one accelerated 90-semester-credit-hour degree aligned to an in-demand career by 2027-28, accredited and meeting reduced-credit requirements, with College Credit Plus pathways; state share of instruction withheld for noncompliance. ORC 3333.97: the Chancellor sets approval criteria, approves each program, and publishes programs and enrollment yearly. Earlier: ORC 3333.43 (2012-2014) required three-year degree statements for 60% of bachelor’s programs, but those are acceleration plans within the full credit total, not reduced credit.
states.framework: ODHE general education guidelines: no fewer than 36 semester hours of general education for baccalaureate, AA and AS degrees; Ohio Transfer 36 (formerly Ohio Transfer Module) of 36 to 40 semester hours is a subset or the whole of each institution’s gen ed, with minimums in English composition, math, arts and humanities, social and behavioral sciences, natural sciences

states.name: Oklahoma
states.label: programs approved at public institutions
states.action: May 2026: OSRHE amended its Academic Program Approval Policy (and Policy 3.15) to create an institutional submission process for workforce-focused bachelor’s degrees of 90 to 119 credit hours (OSRHE release June 1, 2026; two regents voted no), after a feasibility study ordered by Executive Order 2026-08 (presented March 26, 2026) and shared with leaders under HB 3315 (2026). Sept 3, 2026: OSRHE approved four reduced-credit degrees (90 to 103 hours): OU Bachelor of Applied Studies in Social Work; OSU Bachelor of Applied Science in Artificial Intelligence; OSU Bachelor of Applied Science in Business Essentials and Applications; Rogers State Bachelor of Applied Science in Workforce Development.
states.framework: OSRHE basic general education core of at least 40 semester credit hours for every baccalaureate degree (6 English composition, 6 U.S. history and U.S. government, 6 science incl. one lab, 6 humanities, 3 mathematics, 3 guided electives, plus liberal arts and sciences courses to reach 40). Reduced-credit (90 to 119 hour) bachelor’s degrees use a 30-hour general education core (same areas without the extra liberal arts hours).

states.name: Oregon
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No HECC or legislative action on reduced-credit bachelor’s degrees found. Private institutions acted through their accreditor (NWCCU): George Fox University announced Oregon’s first 90-credit (online) bachelor’s in May 2026; Pacific University announced 96-credit three-year programs in July 2026. HECC Executive Director Ben Cannon issued a supportive statement (OPB, May 2026), not a policy action.
states.framework: No statewide general education minimum for the bachelor’s degree. Statewide transfer frameworks only: Oregon Transfer Module (OTM, 45 quarter credits, about 30 semester), Associate of Arts Oregon Transfer (AAOT, 90 quarter credits), Core Transfer Maps (foundational curricula of at least 30 college-level credits under HB 2998, 2017) and Major Transfer Maps.

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No action found by the State Board of Education, Department of Education, PASSHE Board of Governors or the General Assembly on reduced-credit bachelor’s degrees. The 120-credit floor in 22 Pa. Code 31.21 (no amendment since 2013 in the Code current through Aug. 8, 2026) would bar 90-credit degrees at non-community-college institutions without a regulatory change.
states.framework: 22 Pa. Code 31.21(c)(3): of the baccalaureate course requirements, at least 40 semester credit hours (60 quarter) must be general education across a broad spectrum of disciplines (humanities, arts, communications, social sciences, mathematics, technology and science). PASSHE Board Policy 1990-06-A (130.04): at least 40 semester credit hours of general education focused on liberal education competencies, consistent with Policy 1993-01-A. Pennsylvania Statewide Transfer Credit Framework (TAOC): 30 credits of foundational courses in 6 categories that transfer toward general education.

states.name: Rhode Island
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No CPE or legislative action found. Johnson & Wales University (private, Providence) got NECHE approval (Sept 2024) for 90 to 96-credit three-year degrees; that was an accreditor action, not a state action.
states.framework: No statewide general education minimum. CPE Policy for Articulation and Transfer (rev. March 2025) governs the transfer of general education courses among CCRI, RIC and URI; CPE A-4 Regulations Governing Academic Changes require each undergraduate program to include general education (pointing to NECHE Standards 4.14 to 4.18) but set no credit number.

states.name: South Carolina
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No CHE or legislative action on reduced-credit bachelor’s degrees found. SACSCOC (the regional accreditor) adopted a reduced-credit bachelor’s framework (at least 90 semester credit hours) in 2026, which is an accreditor action only.
states.framework: No statewide general education minimum for the bachelor’s degree. Statewide transfer frameworks: Statewide Articulation Agreement of 86 courses and Statewide Transfer Blocks (1996) accepted toward baccalaureate requirements at public four-year institutions (CHE Public Two-Year and Four-Year Transfer Policy, May 2022).

states.name: South Dakota
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No SDBOR or legislative action on reduced-credit or three-year bachelor’s degrees found (searches returned only transfer-credit caps of 90 credits in articulation agreements).
states.framework: System General Education Requirements: 30 credits for every baccalaureate degree, across six goals (written communication 6, oral communication 3, social sciences 6, arts and humanities 6, mathematics 3, natural sciences 6); civics proficiency added from the summer 2025 catalog. Associate degrees: 24 credits.

states.name: Tennessee
states.label: board or system policy adopted
states.action: July 23, 2026: THEC adopted Academic Policy A1.6 Focused Baccalaureate Degrees: Approval Process. Focused Baccalaureate Degrees (FBD) are 90 to 119 SCH (typically 90 to 100), must meet an in-demand workforce need, carry the FBD designation, and need THEC pre-approval before the regular A1.0/A1.1 program process. June 2026: UT Board of Trustees approved a framework for reduced-credit undergraduate degrees across the UT System (each program needs later board approval). Lincoln Memorial University (private) launched a 90-credit B.S. in Education in fall 2026 (news). No THEC approval of a specific public FBD program found as of Oct 2026.
states.framework: 41-semester-hour lower-division general education core common to all public colleges and universities, transferable as a block (Communication 9, Humanities and/or Fine Arts 9, Social/Behavioral Sciences 6, History 6, Natural Sciences 8, Mathematics 3). It is the gen-ed part of the 60-hour Tennessee Transfer Pathways.

states.name: Texas
states.label: proposal, directive or study
states.action: 2026-08-26: Governor Abbott directed THECB to convene a working group and develop a statewide framework for three-year bachelor’s degree pathways (academic standards, fields, accreditation, statutory changes); recommendations due to the Governor by 2026-12-31; the Governor intends to seek legislation in the 90th Legislature (January 2027). Press coverage describes the target as about 90 credits, but the directive itself sets no credit number. No THECB rule or approved 90-credit program found.
states.framework: Texas Core Curriculum: each institution adopts a core of no less than 42 lower-division SCH in THECB foundational component areas; a completed core transfers as a block

states.name: Utah
states.label: programs approved at public institutions
states.action: March 21, 2024: Utah Board of Higher Education created the Bachelor of Applied Studies category with a 90-credit minimum (USHE: first public system in the nation). July 18, 2025: Board applauded the first accelerated (about 90-credit) bachelor’s proposals: Weber State (Sound Production/Recording; Politics, Philosophy, and Economics) and Utah Valley University (Emergency Services Supervision; Professional Advancement), pending NWCCU approval. Weber State’s 90-credit PPE degree launched in fall 2025 (news).
states.framework: Board Policy R470 General Education: each institution’s gen-ed program must require 27 to 30 semester credits: 12 core (6 written communication, 3 quantitative literacy, 3 American Institutions) plus 3 in each of five breadth areas (arts, humanities, life sciences, physical sciences, social and behavioral sciences) = 27, plus up to 3 institutional credits, capped at 30.

states.name: Virginia
states.label: proposal, directive or study
states.action: June 25, 2026: SCHEV announced that Virginia institutions will join Jobs for the Future’s Scaling College in 3 initiative with Ohio, to design a 90-credit three-year bachelor’s model. Institutions aim to propose two 90-credit programs by spring 2028; 11 of 16 public universities and four private colleges have shown preliminary interest (SCHEV spokesperson via news).
states.framework: No statewide bachelor’s gen-ed minimum. Statutory transfer blocks: Passport Program (15 credit hours) inside the 30-credit-hour Uniform Certificate of General Studies (UCGS); each course transfers and satisfies a lower-division general education requirement at any public institution.

states.name: Vermont
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No state or VSC board action on reduced-credit bachelor’s degrees found. UVM’s 3+2 bachelor’s and JD is an accelerated combined program, not a reduced-credit degree.
states.framework: VSC Policy 106 General Education (Aug 12, 2024): every VSC institution must run a gen-ed program covering set areas, with system core competencies and credit-for-credit reciprocity among VSC institutions; no credit minimum.

states.name: Washington
states.label: no state action found
states.action: RCW 28B.10.118 (2011 c 108; 2012 c 229): state universities, regional universities and Evergreen may develop accelerated baccalaureate programs so qualified students can finish in three years without summer classes or overloads; plans go to WSAC for approval. It does not set a reduced credit total. 2025 to 2026: WSU Faculty Senate is considering 90-Credit Bachelor’s (90CB) degrees (90 to 119 semester credits) after NWCCU’s July 2025 change, citing RCW 28B.10.118 as its authority (FAQ, Feb 16, 2026); a final WSU Board of Regents approval was not confirmed.
states.framework: No statewide bachelor’s gen-ed minimum. Statewide transfer block: Direct Transfer Agreement (DTA) associate of 90 quarter credits including 60 quarter credits of general education (about 40 semester); a DTA graduate is deemed to have met the lower-division general education requirements of the receiving four-year institution.

states.name: Wisconsin
states.label: board or system policy adopted
states.action: On March 5, 2026 the Universities of Wisconsin Board of Regents (Education Committee item D, Resolution 12449) amended RPD 4-12 to remove the 120-credit minimum so institutions can develop reduced-credit (90-credit, three-year) bachelor’s degrees, subject to HLC reduced-credit guidelines and substantive change approval; a systemwide working group was set up to recommend implementation policy. New reduced-credit majors need Regents approval; reduced-credit versions of existing programs follow a process similar to other program changes. No specific approved UW 90-credit program was verified.
states.framework: No Board of Regents systemwide general education credit minimum found; each university sets its own. Statutory transfer framework: Wis. Stat. 36.31(2m)(b) requires the Regents and the WTCS board to identify an array of not less than 72 credits of core general education courses that transfer and satisfy general education requirements at the receiving institution (from 2022-23); the earlier Universal Credit Transfer Agreement is a transfer block.

states.name: West Virginia
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No HEPC policy, rule or public-institution program action on reduced-credit bachelor’s degrees found. One unverified online forum post says HEPC and HLC approved a 90-credit cybersecurity bachelor’s at American Public University System (private, Charles Town, WV); this could not be verified (forum 403, no HEPC record found).
states.framework: No statewide bachelor’s gen-ed minimum. Core Coursework Transfer Agreement: up to 35 credit hours of general studies (English composition, communications and literature, fine arts appreciation, mathematics, natural science, social science) transfer as general studies credit among state institutions.

states.name: Wyoming
states.label: no state action found
states.action: No state or UW Board of Trustees action on reduced-credit bachelor’s degrees found. UW’s 3+3 bachelor’s and JD program is an accelerated combined program, not a reduced-credit degree.
states.framework: No statewide gen-ed framework found; UW’s University Studies Program is set by UW.
